title: Customer Support
content: Customer support should first understand the reported issue, verify relevant context, troubleshoot the problem, provide an appropriate resolution, and document the result.

title: IT Support Tickets
content: Support requests can be received through a ticketing system, Microsoft Teams, or direct user requests. The support engineer should understand the issue before selecting remote or physical troubleshooting.

title: Network Troubleshooting
content: For a network issue, check the user's connection, IP configuration, gateway, DNS resolution, and reachability. Useful Windows commands include ipconfig, nslookup, ping, and tracert.

title: System Troubleshooting
content: For Windows system problems, check symptoms, recent changes, Event Viewer logs, application status, and system resources before applying a suitable fix.

title: Hardware Support
content: Hardware support can include checking peripherals such as keyboard and mouse, installing hardware, applying required upgrades, and verifying the system after the change.

title: Security and Privacy
content: Support activities should follow organizational information security and privacy requirements. Sensitive information should only be handled through approved processes.

title: Knowledge Base Limitation
content: The assistant should not invent company-specific facts. When the knowledge base does not contain enough information, it should clearly state that more information is required.
